Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Does a plausible floorplan prove feasibility?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Physical constraints and operating conditions must be checked.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: An AI-generated placement is an input to engineering checks, not a signed-off design. Trace the visual in order: proposal; screening; evidence. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Sketch a proposed chiplet move; list one routing and one thermal check before accepting it.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R10: IEEE EPTC, Thermally Aware Chiplet Placement with RL | https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10909800

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Sketch a proposed chiplet move; list one routing and one thermal check before accepting it. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
